questions.q: What does a Case record represent in Salesforce, per this lesson?
options: A single customer support request or ticket
A closed sales deal
A marketing email campaign
A company-wide announcement
questions.explain: A Case is a single customer question, problem, or request for help — a support ticket, in plain language.

questions.q: What is the Case Number field, per this lesson?
options: A system-generated, sequential, read-only identifier assigned automatically when the Case is created
A field the support rep types in manually for every case
A count of how many cases exist for that Account
The customer's phone number
questions.explain: Case Number is generated by Salesforce the moment the Case is created — it isn't something a user sets.

questions.q: What does the Status field on a Case track?
options: Where the case is in its lifecycle (e.g. New, Working, Escalated, Closed)
Which sales rep sold the original deal
The dollar value of the related Opportunity
The customer's billing address
questions.explain: Status is the single most-used field for support dashboards — 'open cases' means Status isn't in a closed value.

questions.q: What does the Origin field on a Case let an analyst answer, per this lesson?
options: Which support channel (Email, Phone, Web, Chat) generates the most case volume
Which employee owns the case
How much the customer has spent historically
Whether the case is high priority
questions.explain: Origin records the channel the case came in through, which is what lets an analyst report on volume by channel.

questions.q: Why does a Case typically carry lookups to both a Contact and an Account, per this lesson?
options: A support case is tied to a real customer relationship, not a floating standalone record — reporting like 'cases per account' depends on that link
It's a legacy field with no current purpose
Salesforce requires every object to link to every other object
Contacts and Accounts are actually the same object as Case
questions.explain: The lesson ties this directly back to Chapter 2: Cases connect to the Accounts and Contacts already covered, which is what makes account-level case reporting possible.
